title: How do we put a round hole in the middle of each small square?
description: A big square is divided into four equal small squares, and a circle of the same radius is drawn at the centre of each, found where its diagonals meet.
teaching_notes: One idea: the centre of each small square is where its own two diagonals meet, and equal circles come from one compass opening. Watch for students who change the compass opening between circles.

video_script.why: A learner finds the centre of each small square using its diagonals and draws equal circles there.
video_script.substitution: the same way as the example in your book: a circular hole whose centre is the centre of the square
video_script.anchor: a big square divided into four equal small squares, each with a circle in its middle
video_script.payoff_line: Four equal circles sit at the four centres.

final_answer.value: Open ended. Four equal squares, each with a circle of the same radius at its centre, the meeting point of its diagonals

maths_rules: the middle lines divide the big square into 4 equal small squares
the two diagonals of a square meet at its centre
one compass opening gives circles of the same radius
the radius must be small enough for each circle to stay inside its small square
video_script.design: The big square is split into four, the diagonals of each part give its centre, and equal circles are drawn at those centres.
